title: Smooth ascent of punctual purity over a trait
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one and principal maximal ideal; a uniformizer $\pi$ generates that maximal ideal. Suppose $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. Let $X$ be a regular scheme of finite type over $S$, and let $q:Y\to X$ be a smooth finite-type morphism with $Y$ Noetherian [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. If $X$ is punctually pure, then $Y$ is regular and punctually pure.

source.place: Expose XVI Corollary 3.5.6, printed p.249; smooth input follows the diagonal/DNC lecture-notes route.

proof.text: The trait $S$ is Noetherian by its definition, so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $X$ is finite type over $S$. By [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus], smoothness over the regular scheme $X$ makes $Y$ regular. Fix $y\in Y$, and put $x=q(y)$. Choose affine open neighbourhoods $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $x$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $y$ with $q(V)\subset U$. Restriction is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. By [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant], shrink $V$ further to an affine neighbourhood on which this restriction has constant relative dimension $r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $B$ is a finitely generated $C$-algebra, so $V\to U$ is finite type. Replacing $X,Y$ by these opens changes neither local ring at $x,y$ nor its punctual-purity map: these maps are defined on the local schemes themselves. It suffices to prove the assertion at the chosen $y$.

Let $\mathfrak p\subset C$ be the prime of $x$, put $R=C_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $k=\kappa(x)$, and $c=\dim R$. Form $P=V\times_U T$ and $F=P\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k$. Write $h:P\to T$, $i:\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow T$, $a:F\hookrightarrow P$, and $b:F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], the local ring $R$ of the regular scheme $X$ is a regular local ring, hence Noetherian, so $T$ is Noetherian; $T$ is regular because its local rings are the localizations $R_{\mathfrak p'}=\mathcal O_{X,x'}$ at the generizations $x'$ of $x$, which are regular local rings by the same definition. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], $h$ and $b$ are smooth of relative dimension $r$. Finite type is preserved by these base changes [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], so $P$ and $F$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The field $k$ is regular: its only local ring is itself with zero maximal ideal and dimension zero. Thus [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] makes both $P$ and $F$ regular. All these schemes have $\ell$ invertible because their structure maps factor through $X$.

source.place: XVI Corollary 3.5.6, fibrewise expansion; XVI Proposition 3.2.3

proof.text: The immersion $i$ is regular of codimension $c$: choose $c$ generators of the maximal ideal of the regular local ring $R$ using [def-weil-regular-scheme]; they are a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. Since $h$ is smooth, it is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Flat base change in [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] makes $a$ regular of the same constant codimension $c$. Moreover $h$ is a regular morphism in the sense needed for supported base change. Indeed its fibres are smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], remain smooth after every finite field extension by that same statement, and are regular by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus], since a field is regular. These base-changed fibres are Noetherian: finite-type base change [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes them finite type over the extended field, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies. Thus $h$ is flat with geometrically regular fibres. This verifies the hypotheses rather than assuming an excellence property of the trait.

Punctual purity of $X$ at $x$ says that the specified class $\eta_i:A_k\to i^!A_T(c)[2c]$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] to the Cartesian square $(i,a,h,b)$ with exponent $n=1$ and $M=A_T(c)[2c]$. Its Noetherian and regularity hypotheses were verified in Steps 2 and 3. Identifying $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z=A$, it gives the canonical isomorphism
$$b^*i^!A_T(c)[2c]\xrightarrow{\sim}a^!A_P(c)[2c].$$
The twist identification is that of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The closed exceptional functor in the fundamental-class statement agrees on $D^+$ with the supported functor here: for the closed immersions $i$ and $a$ the compactifications $(1,i)$, resp. $(1,a)$, of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] give $Ri_!=i_*$ and $Ra_!=a_*$ (the exact closed direct image applied termwise), so the compact-support right adjoint used by the class is a right adjoint of $i_*$, resp. $a_*$, and it preserves $D^+$ (compute on bounded-below injective representatives); [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] specifies exactly the right adjoint of the same exact closed direct image, obtained by deriving its supported inverse image. Uniqueness of a right adjoint identifies them with their counits. Thus this comparison is the canonical closed-counit comparison, not an arbitrary isomorphism of targets. Flat-base-change compatibility of the specified classes [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] gives
$$\eta_a=B_{h,i}\circ b^*(\eta_i).$$
Both arrows on the right are isomorphisms (a functor preserves inverses), so the pair $(P,F)$ satisfies condition (a) of the two-of-three criterion.

source.place: XVII Corollary 4.2.3, p.281; XVI Theorem 2.3.2, flat-base-change compatibility

proof.text: The regular Noetherian scheme $F$ is a scheme over the field $k$, hence over its prime subfield, which is $\mathbf Q$ in characteristic zero and $\mathbf F_p$ in characteristic $p$. Since $\ell$ is invertible on $F$, [lem-per-prime-field-punctual-purity] applies and proves that $F$ is punctually pure. In particular, this does not assume that $k$ is perfect, or that $F$ is finite type over its prime subfield.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.2.5, p.245; fibre-purity input to Corollary 3.5.6

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] to $a:F\hookrightarrow P$. Both schemes are regular Noetherian with $\ell$ invertible, and $a$ has constant codimension $c$ by Step 3. Step 4 gives its condition (a), and Step 5 gives (b). Therefore (c) holds: $P$ is punctually pure at every point of $F$, in particular at the point $y'$ lying above the chosen $y$ and $x$. This use needs only purity of the fibre and of its closed pair, not purity of $P$ away from the fibre.

Finally the local scheme of $P$ at $y'$ is the local scheme of $Y$ at $y$. Explicitly, let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ represent $y$, so its contraction is $\mathfrak p$, and set $S=C\setminus\mathfrak p$. The maps $B\otimes_C C_{\mathfrak p}\leftrightarrow S^{-1}B$ send $b\otimes(c/s)$ to $bc/s$ and $b/s$ to $b\otimes(1/s)$; these inverse maps respect the tensor relations. Since $S$ misses $\mathfrak q$, localizing this ring at $S^{-1}\mathfrak q$ gives $B_{\mathfrak q}$: $ (b/s)/(b'/s')\mapsto bs'/(sb')$ and $b/b'\mapsto(b/1)/(b'/1)$ are inverse. Thus $\mathcal O_{P,y'}=\mathcal O_{V,y}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with the same residue field, dimension and closed-point pair. Canonical class compatibility under the resulting isomorphism, a flat base change of pairs, is [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. The punctual-purity map at $y'$ in Step 6 is therefore exactly that at $y$ under these identifications. Since $y$ was arbitrary, $Y$ is punctually pure; its regularity was established in Step 1. If $Y$ is empty this conclusion is vacuous. If $c=0$, $i$ and $a$ are identities and their classes are the identity by the codimension-zero clause of the same class-calculus statement.
